definitions.meaning: a fixed habit one has fallen into, as in being stuck in a rut
stands for the spiral channel cut into a vinyl disc, which the stylus follows

explanation.surface: Someone's fixed daily habits are a matter of public record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link: the second sense is the spiral cut into a gramophone record.
explanation.definitionFit: A rut or habitual pattern of life is a groove, and so is the spiral track cut into a disc.

clue.text: Dental problem caused by such sweets?

definitions.text: Dental problem caused by such sweets?

parts.words: Dental problem caused by such sweets?
parts.note: read the name of these chewy jelly sweets as a phrase about gums sagging, a dental complaint the sweets might seem to cause

explanation.surface: A warning that sugary sweets are bad for your teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small sugared jelly confectionery pieces, whose name split in two also describes receding gums.

definitions.meaning: not coloured by personal feeling, i.e. impartial or unbiased
an aim or goal one works towards

explanation.definitionFit: An impartial view is uncoloured by bias, and a goal or aim is also the word as a noun.

indicators.note: the shortened boy is placed into the word for poetry, so this signals one piece going inside another

parts.note: poetry in general is verse

indicators.note: endlessly tells us to cut the last letter off the word boy

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A long-winded lad has got himself mixed up in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wordy boy' reads as a chatty lad, but 'Wordy' is the definition; 'endlessly' trims the boy and 'into' sets him inside the poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Using far more words than needed is being long-winded, the same sense as wordy.

parts.note: something out is not acceptable, as in 'that's right out'
positions of employment are posts

explanation.surface: Nobody wants to be sent to these remote postings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Remote military or trading settlements far from the centre are frontier bases of this kind.

clue.text: Underwear on lines tabu, men resolved

indicators.note: resolved in the sense of broken down and reassembled, so the fodder letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Men's underpants hung out on the washing line are a taboo subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges ONLINESTABUMEN, all fourteen letters of 'on lines tabu men'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coy, jocular term for undergarments, items too delicate to name in polite company.

parts.note: a Victoria is a variety of plum, so this is a definition by example
encountered means met

explanation.surface: Queen Victoria is pictured meeting someone while diving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like a queen or a London station, but here it is the popular British variety of plum.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall or drop steeply and fast is to nosedive, the same as this verb.

clue.text: Young family member chosen for grafting

definitions.meaning: a younger descendant or heir of a notable family
a shoot or twig cut from a plant for grafting onto rootstock

explanation.surface: A youngster of the family has been picked out for hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grafting' suggests British slang for hard work; here it is horticultural.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant or heir is an offspring of a lineage; in gardening the same word means a cutting attached to stock.

indicators.note: placed on board means put aboard a ship, so the word for happily goes inside the ship's letters

parts.note: the ship one is on board is a steamship, abbreviated SS
happily in the sense of satisfactorily or fortunately can mean well

explanation.surface: Dandies are cheerfully seated at the table or on the committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandified, fashionably dressed men of society were called by this slang term, just like dandies.

parts.note: a crossword setter sets clues, but here the features are a face, and the one who sets them is a cosmetic surgeon

explanation.surface: Someone who sets the features of a newspaper, or perhaps of a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosmetic surgeon reshapes noses, chins and other parts of the face, setting them as desired.

definitions.meaning: an army officer ranking above captain

explanation.definitionFit: Something serious or significant is of great consequence; the army rank above captain shares the word.

clue.text: Imposing vehicle holding Finns back in rank

indicators.note: holding means the word for rank contains the other piece inside it

parts.note: a rank is a line, as of soldiers

indicators.note: back says the Finnish name is read in reverse order

parts.note: Suomi is the Finns' own name for their country and people

explanation.surface: A grand car with some Finnish passengers in the back is waiting at the taxi rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Suomi is Finnish for Finland, a fact the solver may not know; 'back' turns it round and 'holding' sets it inside the rank just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A large chauffeur-driven luxury car is an impressive, stately vehicle.

clue.text: Clergymen taking right hand page, reading sermon initially

parts.note: the recto is the right-hand page of an open book

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Priests turn to the right-hand page and read the opening of their sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: RECTO is a printing term for the right-hand page; 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Parish priests in the Church of England holding a living are clergymen of this rank.

clue.text: So-called French name, popular with nearly everybody

parts.note: nom is the French word for name
in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: nearly says the word for everybody loses its last letter

parts.note: everybody is all

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's name is well liked by almost everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: In name only, not in reality, is the sense of a title used loosely or a token amount.

clue.text: Derby, Liverpool and Newcastle, no longer the country's leaders

definitions.text: Derby, Liverpool and Newcastle, no longer the country's leaders

parts.words: Derby, Liverpool and Newcastle, no longer the country's leaders
parts.note: these look like English cities or football clubs, but the Earl of Derby, Lord Liverpool and the Duke of Newcastle were heads of British governments long ago

explanation.surface: Three English football clubs or cities have lost their top-flight status.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby, Liverpool and Newcastle are English cities and football clubs; the clue means the 18th- and 19th-century peers who headed British governments.
explanation.definitionFit: Heads of British government in past centuries included these three titled aristocrats, all now historical figures.

clue.text: Max, we hear, in a cast-iron alternative

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement means the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Someone called Max is apparently living in an iron substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Max, we hear' sounds like macs, British short for mackintoshes; 'alternative' rearranges ACASTIRON; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mackintoshes, commonly shortened to macs, are waterproof coats, and Max sounds just like that word.

indicators.note: over is read as overturned, so the letters of the words that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: In cricket, a six-ball over from a fast seam bowler is scary to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a cricket over; it rearranges OFSEAMER. A seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball deviate off its seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Something terrifying or formidable inspires dread, which is what frightening means.

definitions.meaning: typical of a class, as in a sample that is typical
a commercial traveller, a sales agent on the road

explanation.surface: A trait that is typical of someone who travels.
explanation.walkthrough: A commercial traveller is an old British name for a travelling salesman; 'of a' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Typical of its kind is one sense; a travelling sales agent, often shortened to rep, is the other.

clue.text: Retired, would you say, this soldier of two wars

definitions.meaning: said aloud, retired sounds like re-tyred, a tyre given a new tread
a veteran who served in one world war and re-enlisted for the next

explanation.surface: A veteran of both world wars has finally stood down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' links the two senses. A re-tyred, recapped tyre is one sense; the same word was slang for a veteran recalled to serve again.
explanation.definitionFit: A recapped tyre with new rubber is one meaning; old soldiers called back for a second conflict got the same nickname.

parts.note: like in the sense of in the same way as
'neath is a poetic shortening of beneath, meaning below

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether a word resembles neath, as in Port Talbot's neighbouring Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neath is a poetic shortening of beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart or in pieces, as in torn into two parts, is the sense of split here.

indicators.note: returning means the word for scholars is read backwards

parts.note: school pupils are scholars

explanation.surface: Students make a mistake on their way back to school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns PUPILS backwards; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless mistake or gaffe is a blunder, the same as this informal phrase.

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to ferry cargo to and from ships
a vessel weighs less once its cargo is off

explanation.surface: A vessel is said to have discharged its cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the two: a boat is weighing less once unloaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A barge used for ferrying goods is one sense; weighing less after removing cargo is the comparative adjective.

definitions.meaning: to raven is to eat ravenously, to devour greedily

explanation.surface: Birds such as a raven or swallow feeding in a ravine.
explanation.walkthrough: Raven and swallow look like birds; here they are verbs of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself greedily is to devour; a narrow canyon is the noun sense.

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a short-pitched ball that rears up at the batter's head
a doorman who keeps order at a nightclub

explanation.surface: A threatening parcel arrives for a nightclub worker.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a delivery is a ball bowled; 'for' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A short ball rising sharply at the batter is one sense; a nightclub doorman ejecting troublemakers is the other.

clue.text: Show endurance, by its very nature, ever changing

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself, intrinsically

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the word ever are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Something whose nature is always changing must keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: Per se is a Latin phrase used in English; 'changing' rearranges the four letters of 'ever' to follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is to persist, which is showing endurance.

clue.text: Retired eccentric love of a stern Athenian?

indicators.note: retired, as in withdrawn or gone back, means the word for eccentric is read backwards

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing person
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A retired oddball's sweetheart is a severe man from Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns CARD backwards to DRAC; the 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian lawgiver whose laws were so harsh that the word draconian comes from him.

clue.text: Petitioning for parking at the front

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs
at the front means ahead, in the lead

explanation.surface: Begging for a parking space at the front of the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an earnest appeal or entreaty is begging, the same as petitioning.

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters of the word course are put into the wrong order

explanation.surface: A shipwrecked sailor who went off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges COURSE; 'taking' is a link. Robinson is Defoe's shipwrecked hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Defoe's Robinson is literature's best-known marooned sailor, stranded on an island for years.
